chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to face the Qibla and raise his two hands whenever the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, then say:
O God! Cause it to rise upon us with security, and faith, and wellbeing, and Islam, and encompassing good health, and abundant sustenance, and warding off of illnesses.
O God! Grant us its fasting and its night prayer and recitation of the Quran in it.
O God! Give it to us safely, and receive it back from us safely, and keep us safe in it.

key_terms.اسْتَقْبَلَ الْقِبْلَةَ: Facing the Qibla (direction of the Ka'ba in Mecca) as an act of reverence in supplication
key_terms.الْعَافِيَةُ الْمُجَلِّلَةُ: Encompassing/enveloping good health — health that covers all aspects of one's being
key_terms.صِيَام: Sawm — the ritual fast of Ramadan, abstaining from food, drink and marital relations from dawn to sunset
key_terms.قِيَام: Qiyam al-layl — the voluntary night prayers, especially the Tarawih/Tahajjud in Ramadan
key_terms.هِلَال: The crescent moon marking the beginning of an Islamic lunar month

ai.seo_question: What supplication did the Prophet recite when seeing the crescent of Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) narrates that the Prophet (SAWW) would welcome the crescent of Ramadan with a specific supplication, facing the Qibla with raised hands. This du'a beautifully captures the holistic blessings sought from the blessed month: security, faith, health, sustenance, the ability to fast and pray at night, recite the Quran, and to complete the month in safety. The supplication reflects the Prophet's deep reverence for Ramadan and his desire for his community to receive its full spiritual and physical blessings.
word_analysis: cause it to rise/begin upon us
grant it to us safely/preserve it for us

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Ibrahim Bin Umar Al Yamany, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, whenever it was a crescent of a Month of Ramazan, would face the Qiblah and raise his<sup>saww</sup> hands, so he<sup>saww</sup> would say: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!
Welcome it upon us with the security, and the faith, and the peace, and the Islam, and the good spirited health, and the extensive sustenance, and Repel the illnesses. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!
Grace us its Fasts, and its standing (for the Prayer), and recitation of the Quran therein. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!
Give it as a safety for us, and Receive it back in safety from us, and Keep us safe therein’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Ibrahim ibn ‘Umar al-Yamaniy from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The Messenger of Allah, upon seeing the crescent of the month of Ramadan, would turn toward the Ka‘bah, raise his hands and say, “
O Lord, make it (new moon) a month of peace, belief, safety, submission to the will of Allah, good health with rain, abundant sustenance and without illnesses.
O Lord, grant us the opportunity to fast during this month, perform salat (prayer) and recite the Holy Quran.
O Lord, give it to us with safety, take it back from us with safety, and grant us protection therein.’””
